blocks.text: Head-to-Head Architecture: GP Compact Vertical vs. Scott Pro 4-Roll Coreless

Georgia-Pacific Professional (GP PRO) and Kimberly-Clark Professional dominate the North American coreless bath tissue market. When facility procurement managers weigh the GP Compact Coreless vs. Scott Pro 4-Roll platforms, they are comparing the two most widely supported coreless paper ecosystems in commercial janitorial contracting. Both systems eliminate cardboard cores, outer paper wrappers, and premature stub-roll waste—helping property managers stabilize restroom cleaning allowances ($15 to $30 per restroom per visit) and consumable add-ons ($0.012 to $0.025 per square foot per visit).

The primary physical distinction lies in chassis geometry and roll staging. The Georgia-Pacific Compact Vertical (such as model 56790A / 56784A) stacks two high-density coreless rolls vertically in a slim 6.0-to-7.9-inch wide column, using an automatic drop-down gravity mechanism or a sliding vertical coverplate once the bottom roll is depleted. GP also offers a Compact Quad 4-Roll rotary dispenser, whereas Kimberly-Clark's flagship high-capacity fixture—the Scott Pro High-Capacity Coreless Standard Roll Dispenser—stages four full coreless rolls in a side-by-side or quad-quadrant enclosed cabinet with manual sliding or carousel transfer doors.

blocks.text: Spindle Plug Compatibility: Why GP Compact and Scott Coreless Rolls Do Not Cross-Fit

Facility managers must recognize before signing a multi-year supply agreement that Georgia-Pacific Compact rolls and Kimberly-Clark Scott Pro coreless rolls use incompatible center-mandrel interfaces. Georgia-Pacific Compact rolls feature a small cylindrical center bore that slides over a solid horizontal post or spring-arm inside GP Compact dispensers. By contrast, Kimberly-Clark coreless rolls feature tapered conical dimples on each flat end face of the roll, which snap between spring-loaded conical hubs inside the Scott Pro High-Capacity Coreless Standard Roll Dispenser.

blocks.title: Do Not Mix Coreless Paper Brands Across Floor Plates
blocks.text: If a multi-floor building installs GP Compact Vertical dispensers on Floor 2 and Scott Pro 4-Roll dispensers on Floor 3, night custodians pushing a single restocking barrel will inevitably try to jam conical-dimple Scott rolls onto GP post spindles. Standardize on a single coreless platform building-wide, or use universal cored rolls like Angel Soft Professional Series 2-Ply Embossed Toilet Paper (80-Case, 450 sheets/roll) in executive private restrooms.
Partition Footprint and ADA Stall Geometry

Where the Georgia-Pacific Compact Vertical 2-Roll shines is in older urban office buildings—such as historic financial-district floor plates—where restroom stall doors swing inward with minimal clearance between the toilet bowl and the partition edge. Because the GP Compact Vertical is under 8 inches wide, it mounts cleanly in tight vertical zones forward of the water closet where a 12.75-inch wide 4-roll cabinet or a 19-inch wide twin jumbo JRT dispenser would interfere with a grab bar support bracket or stall door latch.

blocks.text: Custodial Restocking Math: 2-Roll Vertical vs. 4-Roll Quad Capacity

To decide whether a 2-roll GP Compact Vertical or a 4-roll Scott Pro Coreless makes better financial sense, calculate your building's sheet consumption between scheduled janitorial visits. The average office worker uses approximately 25 to 35 sheets of 2-ply bath tissue per workday. In an 80-person office floor with four toilet stalls (20 employees per stall), each stall dispenses roughly 550 sheets per day.

With a GP Compact Vertical 2-Roll loaded with two 1,500-sheet 2-ply rolls (3,000 sheets total), each stall holds 5.4 business days of tissue. With a Scott Pro 4-Roll loaded with four 1,150-sheet 2-ply rolls (4,600 sheets total), each stall holds 8.3 business days of tissue. That extra 3-day buffer means an office running a 1x-weekly (4.33 visits/month, 1.08x rate multiplier) or 2x-weekly (8.66 visits/month, 1.00x base rate) cleaning contract can depend on the 4-roll system to survive surge occupancy days without running out on Thursday afternoon.

items.name: Step 1: Measure Available Horizontal Partition Space Forward of the Toilet
items.text: Check for at least 14 inches of unobstructed horizontal space 7 to 9 inches ahead of the water closet rim before ordering a 4-roll quad cabinet. If horizontal space is under 11 inches, specify the GP Compact Vertical 2-Roll.

items.name: Step 2: Align Sheet Capacity with Your Cleaning Frequency Multiplier
items.text: For 5x-weekly daily weekday service (21.65 visits/month), a 2-roll vertical coreless dispenser easily holds 4 to 5 days of buffer. For 1x-weekly or 2x-weekly schedules, choose a 4-roll coreless system to prevent mid-week outages.

items.name: Step 3: Audit Consumable Pricing Per 1,000 Sheets
items.text: Compare case pricing by dividing total case cost by total sheets per case (e.g., 36 rolls x 1,000 sheets = 36,000 sheets) rather than cost per roll, since coreless rolls hold double the sheets of standard cored tissue.

faqs.q: Can I fit Scott Pro coreless toilet paper rolls inside a Georgia-Pacific Compact dispenser?
faqs.a: No. Georgia-Pacific Compact rolls have a continuous hollow center hole that slides over a mounting spindle post, whereas Scott Pro coreless rolls have solid ends with recessed conical dimples held by spring-loaded side clips. Always match the paper refill brand to the mounted dispenser chassis.

faqs.q: How does GP Compact Vertical auto-drop work when the bottom roll runs out?
faqs.a: In GP Compact Vertical sliding-gate models, the user slides the front shield upward once the lower roll is completely empty, exposing the upper reserve roll. In gravity-drop configurations, removing the spent lower roll allows the top reserve roll to drop into the primary dispensing cradle so the custodian always loads the fresh roll into the top reserve slot.

faqs.q: Do coreless toilet paper dispensers comply with ADA single-hand operation rules?
faqs.a: Yes. Both the GP Compact Vertical and Scott Pro 4-Roll dispensers are compliant with ADA Standards Section 309.4 when mounted at proper reach heights (15 to 48 inches above the floor, 7 to 9 inches in front of the bowl), as their sliding transfer doors require less than 5 pounds of force and zero tight grasping, pinching, or wrist twisting.

faqs.q: How much storage closet space do coreless cases save compared to 80-roll standard cases?
faqs.a: A 36-roll case of high-capacity coreless bath tissue delivers roughly the same total sheet count as an 80-roll case of standard cored tissue (36,000 sheets) while occupying up to 45% less shelf volume and eliminating 80 cardboard tubes and 80 paper outer wrappers per case.
